properties.digitized_from: DataSF Building Footprints dataset (real, surveyed building outline; not tied to an Assessor parcel).
properties.digitization_method: ADDED 2026-09-17 to fix a major, previously-unaddressed real-vs-approximate overlap: this project's status.csv had 'Building 14' joined to blklot 4052001, a giant (~134,945 sq m / ~33-acre) Assessor lot that turns out to underlie almost the ENTIRE eastern two-thirds of the Pier 70 site -- overlapping essentially every D4D approximate parcel there (A, B, D, E1-E4, 21, F/G, H1, H2, Waterfront Open Space, Building 12 Plaza, even Irish Hill Playground), not just Building 14's own footprint. A user noticed persistent visual overlap on the rendered map and asked directly whether the same validation process was being used as elsewhere; investigating with a from-scratch real-vs-approximate overlap check (which this project's check_geometry_quality.py had never actually performed -- it only ever checked approximate-vs-approximate sibling overlaps) surfaced this. The Pier 70 labeled map had separately excluded 4052001 from its own rendering (2026-09-17, 'Always show Building 12' commit) for being oversized, but that was a rendering-only patch on the Pier70-specific map -- it did nothing for the citywide static/interactive maps, which were still rendering 4052001's full extent, and did nothing about the underlying data conflict. ROOT-CAUSE FIX: matched Building 14 to its own specific real footprint the same way Buildings 101/102/104/113-116/21 were already split out of their own oversized blklots. Figure 6.4.2's own '14' label box (pixel bounds ~(947,505)-(1073,613) on page171.png) transforms to real-world centroid lon -122.38532, lat 37.76029; the nearest candidate footprint under mblr=SF4052001 (1556.6 sq m / ~16,754 sqft) sits 39m away -- and its size is a near-exact match (within 3%) to status.csv's own previously-cited '16,315 gsf double-gable metal warehouse' figure for Building 14, which is strong independent confirmation this is the right footprint. Confirmed 0 overlap against the 113/114/115/116 complex (2.1m gap, essentially touching, consistent with the diagram showing them as adjacent structures), Parcel D, Parcel C1, PKN, the 20th Street Plaza, and the Waterfront Open Space. 2026-09-29 accuracy audit: the footprint above is under legacy id mblr SF4052001 / blklot 4052001, which DataSF retired on 2018-10-02 (acdm-wktn; 21 footprints carry that id), so it is not a current Assessor lot and does not by itself identify Building 14; the identification rests on position and size as described above. The footprint now falls within active lot 4111008 (no street address). Nothing in the geometry was changed.
properties.accuracy_caveat: REAL, surveyed building footprint (DataSF Building Footprints) -- high confidence in the outline itself and its match to Building 14: position matches Figure 6.4.2's own label (39m away, the closest and only plausible candidate among the lot's other footprint pieces once 113/114/115/116's own pieces are excluded) and its area independently matches the previously-cited 16,315 GSF within 3%. As with the other buildings split from oversized Assessor lots this project, the match rests on position and size, not an explicit building-number attribute in the footprint dataset itself (no such attribute exists there).
properties.why_no_real_parcel: This structure has no street address in DataSF's Assessor roll and no distinct Assessor lot of its own. Its footprint lay about 76% on the former lot blklot 4052001 and about 24% on former lot 4111003, both retired by DataSF on 2018-10-02; it now falls within active lot 4111008 (no street address, shared with Buildings 113-116). The 2013 HPC packet lists Block 4046 Lot 001, Block 4111 Lots 003 and 004 and a portion of Block 4052 Lot 001 as the project location for the ten historic buildings; the earlier statement that Buildings 101/102/104/113-116/21 shared one lot with Building 14 is withdrawn (101/102/104 lay on 4046001 and 113-116 on 4111004). This feature uses the real building footprint instead, matched individually.
properties.regulatory_context: Building 14, a basic heavy warehouse dated to 1941 (per the 2013 HPC packet, 2013.1168E) with approximately 16,000 GSF of space and a 66 foot height, sits immediately east of the Union Iron Works Machine Shop complex (Buildings 113/114/115/116), framing, with them, an approximately 45,000 square foot courtyard per the 2013 HPC packet's rehabilitation concept (not the D4D). Rehabbed by Orton Development Inc. (ODI) as part of the same 20th Street Historic Core project; proposed for the same industrial/warehouse/maker-space use (food, tech, life science, biotech, education, arts production) with ancillary office, showroom, and retail as its neighbors.
properties.notes: Split 2026-09-17 from the oversized combined blklot 4052001 row -- see digitization_method. This resolves a major real-vs-approximate overlap that had gone undetected because check_geometry_quality.py only ever checked approximate-vs-approximate sibling overlaps, never real-vs-approximate ones.
